UPSTREAM: drm/amdkfd: Disable CP/SDMA ring/doorbell in MQD The MQD represents an inactive context and should not have ring or doorbell enable bits set. Doing so interferes with HWS which streams the MQD onto the HQD. If enable bits are set this activates the ring or doorbell before the HQD is fully configured. UPSTREAM: drm/amdkfd: Avoid calling amd_iommu_unbind_pasid() when suspending When kfd suspending on APU, we do not need to call amd_iommu_unbind_pasid(), because pasid will be unbound automatically when power goes off. On the other hand, calling amd_iommu_unbind_pasid() will trigger kfd_process_iommu_unbind_callback() if the process is not terminating. By design, kfd_process_iommu_unbind_callback() should only be called for process terminating. So we would rather not to call amd_iommu_unbind_pasid() when suspending. BUG=b:65489307 TEST=boot Kahlee, run graphics_SanAngeles Signed-off-by: Yong Zhao <yong.zhao@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Felix Kuehling <Felix.Kuehling@amd.com> Reviewed-by: Oded Gabbay <oded.gabbay@gmail.com> Signed-off-by: Oded Gabbay <oded.gabbay@gmail.com> (cherry picked from commit e2a8e99964ded3a156137c1a02832493ee727721) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ibbc9252214b245b0d7d817aa4b80d92abdcde883 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/807094 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu/virt: don't dereference undefined 'module' struct Accessing the THIS_MODULE directly is only possible when modules are enabled, otherwise we get a build failure: drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_virt.c: In function 'amdgpu_virt_init_data_exchange': drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_virt.c:331:20: error: dereferencing pointer to incomplete type 'struct module' Further, THIS_MODULE is NULL when the driver is built-in, so the code would likely cause a NULL pointer dereference. This adds an #ifdef check to avoid the compile-time error, plus a NULL pointer check before dereferencing THIS_MODULE. It might be better to find a way to avoid using the module version altogether. Fixes: 2dc8f81e4f82 ("drm/amdgpu: SR-IOV data exchange between PF&VF") BUG=b:65489307 TEST=boot Kahlee, run graphics_SanAngeles Signed-off-by: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> Reviewed-by: Harry Wentland <harry.wentland@amd.com> Reviewed-By: Xiangliang Yu <Xiangliang.Yu@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit e477e940dad1836c6f6d23353e424665b9316b6e) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ifabab2a8ffb16fc6e1c34fea90e519c8ceeb7359 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/807100 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/ttm: Downgrade pr_err to pr_debug for memory allocation failures Memory allocation failure should generally be handled gracefully by callers. In particular, with transparent hugepage support, attempts to allocate huge pages can fail under memory pressure, but the callers fall back to allocating individual pages instead. In that case, there would be spurious [TTM] Unable to get page %u error messages in dmesg.
